title: Schedule K-1 and basis — Oakline Partners
instructions: Maya is a 40% general partner in Oakline Partners, a calendar-year partnership. Compute the partnership's ordinary business income, Maya's K-1 amounts, and her ending basis.

exhibits.title: Oakline's 2025 results
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Sales | 600,000 |
| Cost of goods sold | 250,000 |
| Operating expenses (salaries, rent, depreciation) | 110,000 |
| Guaranteed payment to Maya for services | 30,000 |
| §1231 gain | 20,000 |
| Long-term capital gain | 15,000 |
| Dividends | 5,000 |
| Charitable contributions | 10,000 |
| Tax-exempt interest | 4,000 |
| §179 expense | 12,000 |

exhibits.title: Maya's basis information
exhibits.content:
- Basis at January 1, 2025: **$60,000**
- Her share of partnership liabilities increased by **$10,000** during 2025
- Cash distributions to Maya (other than the guaranteed payment): **$70,000**

rows.label: Maya's share of ordinary business income
Maya's self-employment income from Oakline before her §179 share (ordinary income share + guaranteed payment)
rows.explanation: 84,000 + 30,000 guaranteed payment = **114,000** (general partner). On Schedule SE her §179 share then reduces it to 109,200 (K-1 box 14 net earnings).

rows.label: Ending basis at December 31, 2025
rows.explanation: 60,000 + 84,000 + 8,000 + 6,000 (LTCG) + 2,000 (dividends) + 1,600 (exempt interest) + 10,000 (liabilities) − 4,000 (charity) − 4,800 (§179) − 70,000 (distributions) = **92,800**. The guaranteed payment doesn't change basis.

rows.label: Is Maya taxed on the $70,000 cash distribution?
options: No — it's less than her basis
rows.answer: No — it's less than her basis
rows.explanation: Current distributions are tax-free to the extent of outside basis.

rows.label: Where does Maya report her share of the charitable contributions?
options: As an itemized deduction on her own return
As a reduction of ordinary business income
rows.answer: As an itemized deduction on her own return
